@@ -0,0 +1,211 @@ +--- +// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 +// +// "Linting & migration" — the guide to keeping templates canonical and importing +// Handlebars. Two user-facing tools: `flatbars lint` (warn-only canonicalization, +// for editors and CI) and `flatbars migrate` (Handlebars → MaxBars source, with a +// residual report). Unlike the dialect references this is a CLI/CI guide, not an +// interactive playground — the linter has no Lab view, so the before/after here is +// the exact tool output, gate-validated against the engine (../lint.mjs, gated by +// scripts/check-tutorial-tooling.mjs). The normative text lives in docs/ +// (adr-0019-operation-vocabulary, adr-0021-maxbars-variable-model). +import Reference from "../layouts/Reference.astro"; +import { lintExamples, migrateExamples } from "../lint.mjs"; + +const t = (s) => s; // readability helper for inline tag literals + +const groups = [ + { + label: "Linting & migration", + items: [ + { href: "#intro", label: "What the linter does" }, + { href: "#aliases", label: "Deprecated aliases" }, + { href: "#scoped", label: "Scoped variables" }, + { href: "#ci", label: "In the editor & CI" }, + { href: "#migrate", label: "Migrating Handlebars" }, + { href: "#residuals", label: "What migration can't do" }, + { href: "#library", label: "Lower & lift (library)" }, + ], + }, + { + label: "Other references", + items: [ + { href: "/analyse", label: "Truthiness portability" }, + { href: "/maxbars", label: "MaxBars" }, + { href: "/fullbars", label: "FullBars" }, + ], + }, + { + label: "Play", + items: [{ href: "/lab/index.html?engine=maxbars", label: "FlatBars Lab ↗" }], + }, +]; +--- + + + + + +
+

What the linter does

+

+ The engine accepts more than one spelling for the same thing: a few deprecated + aliases (plus for add), and legacy spellings of the + loop scoped variables (index for index0). They render + identically — so this is never a render error and never blocks output. It is a + hygiene check: flatbars lint emits one warning per non-canonical + use, pointing at the canonical name, for your editor to surface and your CI to gate. +

+

+ A separate tool, flatbars migrate, is a one-shot + Handlebars → MaxBars source rewriter for importing existing templates. +

+
+ + +
+

Deprecated aliases

+

+ An alias is a second name the prelude still installs but no longer prefers. The lint + points at the canonical name; the migrate/lift assist can rewrite + it for you. +

+
+ template + 
{lintExamples.alias.template}
+ flatbars lint + 
{lintExamples.alias.report}
+
+
+ + +
+

Scoped variables

+

+ Inside a loop, the canonical names in RawBars/MaxBars are index0, + rindex0, first, last, key; the bare + index/rindex/size are legacy spellings. The lint + steers you to the canonical one. +

+
+ template + 
{lintExamples.scopedVariable.template}
+ flatbars lint --maxbars + 
{lintExamples.scopedVariable.report}
+
+

+ This lint is surface-scoped: it runs for RawBars/MaxBars, where the bare native + name is canonical, but not for FullBars — there {t("{{@index}}")} + is the Handlebars spelling and stays canonical. Run it with --surface and + only the alias lint applies. +

+
+ + +
+

In the editor & CI

+

+ In your editor — the FlatBars language server (VS Code, JetBrains) surfaces each + finding as a diagnostic with a one-click quick-fix that rewrites the name to its + canonical form. The replacement comes from the same prelude the linter reads, so the + editor and the CLI can never disagree. +

+

+ In CI — a clean template says so, and --max-warnings turns findings + into a gate (default 0: any finding fails the build): +

+ 
$ flatbars lint template.rawbars
+{lintExamples.clean.report}
+
+$ flatbars lint src/email.maxbars --maxbars --max-warnings 0   # CI gate
+
+ + +
+

Migrating Handlebars

+

+ flatbars migrate rewrites Handlebars source to MaxBars, touching only the + tags that change and slicing the rest from the original — so spacing and + whitespace-control survive. The mechanical rewrites: +

+ +

@-data → the loop object

+
+ 
{migrateExamples.loopVars.template}
+ migrate ↓ + 
{migrateExamples.loopVars.source}
+
+ +

Inverted section → {t("{{#unless}}")}

+
+ 
{migrateExamples.inverted.template}
+ migrate ↓ + 
{migrateExamples.inverted.source}
+
+ +

Block-partial reference → {t("{{yield}}")}

+
+ 
{migrateExamples.partialBlock.template}
+ migrate ↓ + 
{migrateExamples.partialBlock.source}
+
+
+ + +
+

What migration can't do

+

+ Migration is honest about its limits: where a Handlebars construct has no single + meaning in MaxBars, it leaves the source unchanged and reports a residual + for a human to resolve — it never guesses. +

+
+ 
{migrateExamples.ambiguousSection.template}
+ migrate ↓ (unchanged) + 
{migrateExamples.ambiguousSection.source}
+
+
+ Residual · ambiguous-section. A bare Mustache section {t("{{#widget}}")} + renders its body when widget is truthy and iterates when it is a + list — MaxBars splits those into distinct shapes. + Choose the intended form: {t("{{#if widget}}…{{/if}}")} + for a truthy guard, or {t("{{#each widget}}…{{/each}}")} to iterate. +
+

+ The other residual is set-delimiters ({t("{{=<% %>=}}")}): MaxBars + has no delimiter switching, so it is reported, not rewritten. +

+
+ + +
+

Lower & lift (library)

+

+ Two more transforms exist as library functions, not CLI commands, because they + are round-trip plumbing rather than everyday tasks: lower prints a MaxBars + template as the equivalent austere RawBars core source, and + lift heuristically re-sugars core source back to MaxBars (flagging the + ambiguous spots). They are the proof that the surface desugaring is reversible; reach + for them from the linter package, not the terminal. +

+
+
